name: Clarified Sugar Syrup
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: the best double-refined loaf-sugar
ingredients.originalText: eight pounds of the best double-refined loaf-sugar

ingredients.name: two quarts of very clear spring or pump water
ingredients.originalText: two quarts of very clear spring or pump water
ingredients.quantityText: two quarts of very clear spring or pump water

instructions.text: Break up or powder the eight pounds of sugar
Beat the whites of four eggs to a strong froth
Stir the white of egg gradually into two quarts of very clear spring or pump water
Put the sugar into a porcelain kettle and mix with it the water and white of egg
While the sugar is melting, stir it frequently
When it is entirely dissolved, put the kettle over a moderate fire and let it boil
Carefully take off the scum as it comes to the top
Pour in a little cold water when you find the syrup rising so as to run over the edge of the kettle
When it first boils hard, pour in half a pint of cold water to keep down the bubbles so that the scum may appear and be easily removed

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Break up or powder the eight pounds of sugar
2. Beat the whites of four eggs to a strong froth
3. Stir the white of egg gradually into two quarts of very clear spring or pump water
4. Put the sugar into a porcelain kettle and mix with it the water and white of egg
5. While the sugar is melting, stir it frequently
6. When it is entirely dissolved, put the kettle over a moderate fire and let it boil
7. Carefully take off the scum as it comes to the top
8. Pour in a little cold water when you find the syrup rising so as to run over the edge of the kettle
9. When it first boils hard, pour in half a pint of cold water to keep down the bubbles so that the scum may appear and be easily removed
